title: Energy Standard for Sites and Buildings Except Low-Rise Residential Buildings

sections.title: General — Scope of Lighting Requirements
sections.text: Section 9 applies to interior and exterior lighting systems in all buildings covered by the standard. Lighting power limits apply to all permanently installed lighting, including general illumination, decorative lighting, and lighting in mechanical rooms and stairwells. Exceptions include emergency lighting that operates only on backup power, lighting in spaces specifically exempted by Section 9.2, and lighting in dwelling units.

sections.title: Exemptions
sections.text: The following lighting is exempt from the interior lighting power limits: (1) emergency lighting that has dual-switching capability operating only on emergency backup power, (2) decorative gas lighting systems, (3) lighting in dwelling units, (4) lighting equipment that is for sale or being demonstrated in lighting showrooms, (5) lighting equipment used in agricultural applications. Note: Exit signs are not exempt from the standard even though they are required by life safety codes.

sections.title: Interior Lighting Controls — Automatic Shutoff
sections.text: All interior lighting in buildings larger than 5,000 sq ft must have automatic shutoff controls. Acceptable methods include: (1) occupancy sensor that turns lights off within 30 minutes of occupancy ceasing, (2) scheduled automatic shutoff that turns lights off at specific times, (3) signal from another control or building automation system. Occupancy sensors must also comply: in spaces where automatic partial-off is used instead of full shutoff, lights must reduce to at least 50% power within 30 minutes of vacancy.

sections.title: Space Controls — Occupancy Sensing
sections.text: Occupancy sensors are required in the following space types: offices 250 sf or smaller, classrooms and lecture halls, conference/meeting rooms, employee lunch and break rooms, storage rooms, janitorial closets, restrooms, locker rooms. For spaces 250 sf or smaller the sensor must control all lighting in the space. Manual-on sensors (vacancy sensors) are preferred over auto-on in private offices and other enclosed spaces where occupants can manually turn on lights.

sections.title: Daylight Controls — Mandatory Sidelighting and Toplighting
sections.text: Daylight-responsive controls are required in: (1) all primary sidelighted areas of 120 sf or more where the total installed lighting power is 150 W or more, (2) all daylit areas under skylights of 900 sf or more where the total installed lighting power is 150 W or more, (3) all primary sidelighted areas in addition to those in item 1 that are 900 sf or more. Daylight controls must reduce electric lighting by at least 50% or maintain illuminance set point within 10% under sufficient daylight conditions.

sections.title: Decorative Lighting Controls
sections.text: Decorative and display lighting, including case lighting, and lighting in hotel lobbies, must be separately switched from general illumination and must be controlled by a time-of-day schedule or occupancy sensor. This allows decorative lighting to be turned off during periods of no occupancy while maintaining general illumination if needed.

sections.title: Hotel and Motel Guest Room Controls
sections.text: Each hotel and motel guest room must have at least one master control at the main entrance that controls all permanently installed luminaires and switched receptacles. This master control must automatically turn off all loads within 20 minutes of the guest leaving the room, which may be accomplished by a key card switch, door sensor, or occupancy sensor. All bathroom lighting must be controlled separately from the bedroom.

sections.title: Exit Signs
sections.text: All exit signs must use LED sources or equivalent with a maximum of 5 watts per face. Illuminated exit signs that use more than 5 W per face are not compliant. This applies to internally illuminated exit signs; externally illuminated exit signs are exempt from the 5W limit but must comply with IBC requirements. Exit signs in compliance with this section do not count toward the building's interior LPD allowance.

sections.title: Interior Lighting Power Allowance — Space-by-Space Method
sections.text: The Space-by-Space Method calculates the interior lighting power allowance by multiplying the LPD allowance for each space type by the area of that space. The total allowance is the sum of all space allowances. This method is preferred when a building has many different space types. LPD allowances are listed in Table 9.5.1. Spaces not listed must use the LPD of the most similar space type or default to 0.82 W/ft² (office).

sections.title: Building Area Method — Interior LPD
sections.text: The Building Area Method allows a single LPD allowance applied to the entire building gross square footage. It is simpler but typically less flexible than the Space-by-Space Method. The total LPD cannot exceed the value in Table 9.6.1 for the building type. If a building contains multiple uses, the building type is the predominant use by floor area.

sections.title: Exterior Lighting Controls
sections.text: All exterior lighting must be controlled by a combination of a photosensor and a time switch, or an astronomical time switch. The photosensor must turn lights on at dusk and off at dawn. The time switch provides additional control for reducing lighting during late-night hours. Façade and landscape lighting must be turned off between midnight and 6 AM or when the building is not in use, whichever is later.

sections.title: Exterior Lighting Power Allowance
sections.text: Exterior lighting power is calculated using a base allowance plus tradeable and non-tradeable allowances based on exterior zones (E1-E4 per ASHRAE/IESNA). The total exterior LPD is limited based on the lighting zone designation of the site. Trade-off between exterior zones is not permitted. Non-tradeable allowances apply to specific features such as vehicle canopies, walkways, sales lots, and building facades.

sections.title: Lighting Power Compliance — Allowed Adjustments
sections.text: Additional LPD allowances are permitted for: (1) additional 1.0 W/ft² for retail display lighting beyond the base space allowance, (2) hotel and motel guest rooms get an additional 0.35 W/ft² when supplemental heat lamps are installed in bathrooms, (3) specific task lighting connected to switched receptacles (less than 0.3 W/ft²) may be excluded if it is plug-in and not permanently installed. Supplemental task lighting at workstations is included in the LPD calculation when it is hardwired.

sections.title: Lighting Controls — Multi-level Capability
sections.text: All interior lighting must be capable of being reduced to at least 50% power through any of the following methods: (1) daylight-responsive controls, (2) occupancy/vacancy sensing, (3) manual continuous dimming, (4) multi-level switching (at least 2 steps where one is ≤50%). Exceptions: single-occupant spaces controlled by occupancy sensor, spaces where multi-level would endanger safety, and emergency lighting.
